items.title: Bystanders help save driver from sinking car in Guelph Lake
items.summary: Bystanders helped to save a driver from a sinking vehicle in Guelph Lake on Wednesday, police say. , Wellington County OPP officers and other emergency services responded to a vehicle that had driven off Wellington Road 124 and landed in Guelph Lake. Police said later details revealed that the driver was trapped inside the car and it was sinking. “While arriving on scene, numerous Good Samaritans from nearby stopped vehicles were observed already in the lake assisting the trapped driver from the submerged sedan,” OPP said. ” A guard rail was damaged in the incident. No other vehicles were involved. Wellington Road 124 and Jones Baseline were closed in the area after the collision as officers investigated. Police didn’t say what may have been the cause.

items.title: 71 vehicles broken into in Mississauga; man faces dozens of charges
items.summary: A man faces dozens of charges after 71 vehicles were broken into in Mississauga earlier this month, resulting in “significant property damage and financial losses for residents,” police say. “The incidents occurred during the early morning hours of Sept. 3 and Sept. 6, and targeted neighbourhoods throughout Mississauga,” Peel Regional Police said on Thursday. Investigators said the nearly six dozen vehicles were targeted by a culprit who either smashed car windows or entered through unlocked doors before stealing valuables. “While no vehicles were stolen and all vehicles were unoccupied at the time, the incidents resulted in significant property damage and financial losses for residents,” police said in a news release. Subsequent investigation by officers with the Peel police 11 Division Criminal Investigation Bureau led to the arrest of a suspect. ” Cory Lowden, 34, of no fixed address, is charged with: He was also arrested for two outstanding warrants related to separate fraud investigations, police noted, adding the accused was held in custody pending a bail hearing.

items.title: Funding boost for paramedics, ambulance service in Ontario region
items.summary: Ambulance service in Durham Region earned a financial boost of nearly $41 million from the province this week to connect more people to emergency care faster and increase the availability of paramedics and ambulances in the community. Ontario is increasing land ambulance funding by 10 per cent, bringing the province’s total investment in the region to $40,247,775 this year, an increase in base funding that helps ensure municipalities address increased costs so they can continue to deliver high-quality emergency care. The province is also investing $742,616 in the Dedicated Offload Nurses program to reduce delays paramedics encounter when arriving at hospitals to transfer patients. The funds will be used to hire nurses and other eligible health professionals dedicated to offloading ambulance patients in hospital emergency departments. 9 million investment will help Durham Region continue to deliver high-quality emergency care by supporting frontline paramedic services and reducing ambulance offload delays in our hospitals,” said Ontario Finance Minister and Pickering-Uxbridge MPP Peter Bethlenfalvy. ” This investment is part of the more than $1 billion in land ambulance funding Ontario is providing municipalities across the province this year, representing an average increase of nine per cent from 2025. “During life’s most challenging moments, residents need to know help will be there when they call. This increase to our provincial Land Ambulance Service Grant funding and Dedicated Offload Nurses program recognizes the growing needs of our communities,” said Region of Durham Chair John Henry. The Dedicated Offload Nurses program allows paramedics to get back out into the community faster and respond to their next 9-1-1 call sooner and has played a significant role in reducing ambulance offload times and increasing ambulance availability for 9-1-1 patients across the province.

items.title: Support is moving closer to home for some Brampton cancer patients
items.summary: For people going through cancer treatment, getting support does not always mean another trip to a hospital or specialized health-care facility. Now, some of that support is coming to neighbourhood community spaces across Brampton. Wellspring Chinguacousy is expanding its free cancer exercise and movement programs beyond its cancer support centre, bringing services to Century Gardens Recreation Centre and the Cyril Clark Library Branch. The expansion is being supported by a $475,900 Ontario Trillium Foundation grant that will fund the initiative over the next three years. For Wellspring, the change is about making it easier for cancer patients and their families to access support during what can be a physically and emotionally difficult time. “We provide services to about 600 families annually, and this expansion will enable us to reach more cancer patients and enhance access to our programs,” Wellspring Chinguacousy executive director Rebecca Harrison said. ” Cancer Exercise is being offered at Century Gardens Recreation Centre, while Tai Chi and Yoga programs are being offered at the Cyril Clark Library Branch. The programs are part of Wellspring’s broader approach to helping people deal with the physical, emotional, social and practical challenges that can accompany a cancer diagnosis.

items.title: Giant used book sale returns to Mississauga for four days
items.summary: One of the largest used book sales in Ontario takes place over four days starting Thursday in Mississauga. Book lovers are expected once again to flock to the Mississauga Symphony Orchestra’s Giant Used Book Sale, taking place tonight through Sunday on the lower level at Sherwood Village (formerly known at various times over the decades as Sheridan Centre and Sheridan Mall). Considered among the largest such events in Ontario, the book sale is back for its 31st year in the city. ” The Mississauga Symphony Orchestra’s Giant Used Book Sale features thousands of fiction and non-fiction titles, vinyl records, CDs, DVDs, puzzles, board games and sheet music. “All items are in excellent condition and listed at unbeatable prices,” book sale organizers said in a news release. , just north of the QEW. Organizers note the book sale is a cash-only event with proceeds going to support the MSO’s annual concert season, the rapidly growing Mississauga Symphony Youth Orchestra and special large-scale projects such as fully-staged opera.

items.title: Don’t let water quality go down the drain this pool season
items.summary: Getting ready to close your outdoor pool? A few simple steps can help keep chemicals out of the stormwater system and protect Lake Ontario, the source of Mississauga's drinking water. Many Mississauga homes have backyard pools that need to be drained and winterized before colder weather arrives. If you’re closing your outdoor pool for the winter, it’s important to do it safely and responsibly. Prevent pool chemicals from entering waterways and harming wildlife by disposing of them the right way. This helps protect your health and our environment. Remove leaves, grass and other debris from the water. This helps keep the water cleaner over the winter. If you have an automatic pool cleaner, remove it, drain it, let it dry and store it until next season. Test the pool water for chlorine and pH levels. 0, which is neutral. After treatment, do not add any more chemicals or algae-control products for at least seven days. Before draining any water, make sure the chlorine level is zero. Pool and spa owners must follow the City of Mississauga’s by-law when draining water.

items.title: Mississauga taking action on tariffs: City exploring additional business supports as trade uncertainty continues
items.summary: A range of business competitiveness and resilience measures, including tax relief, economic development and procurement initiatives and development-related tools will be explored. Economic Development | September 16, 2026 As Canada responds to the latest trade measures from the United States that include new tariffs and import restrictions affecting key sectors of the economy, City Council approved a motion today to direct staff to explore a range of support measures for businesses affected by tariffs. The motion directs City staff to review and report to back to Council on: The motion follows an update to Council at the City’s General Committee meeting on September 9 about the impact of trade tariffs. The update focused on the key role Partners in Trade plays in the current trade climate. Watch the video from the September 9 General Committee meeting. See the PowerPoint presentation. In an effort to strengthen local economic resilience, protect jobs and alleviate financial pressure for local businesses and workers in Mississauga, the review will examine potential tax relief programs, investment and economic development initiatives, planning incentives, grant opportunities and procurement strategies, with recommendations to be presented to Council at a future meeting. As Ontario’s second largest economy and key contributor to the federal government’s Build Canada priority, Mississauga is taking action to help businesses respond to trade uncertainty, compete in new markets and strengthen long-term growth. Through Partners in Trade, the City is focused on connecting businesses to opportunities, advocating for local priorities and building a more resilient economy.
